posts.author: Timothius
posts.body:
Hello! I am hoping someone can help me. When the characters in my game score a critical hit, there is still a chance no damage happens. I come from D&D mentality where critical means automatic hit and damage multiplied.
I got the impression from a number of sources that the only way to fix this is in the damage formula. If so, here is my normal attack formula:
((4 * a.atk ** 2) / (a.atk + b.def)) / 2
How do I update this to make it so a critical hit will always get through and do the damage it is supposed to do?
Alternatively, is there a different way to make criticals always hit and always do damage?

That's a very interesting formula. I've never seen anyone use exponent calculation for the damage.
At least I think the ** is exponent.
So you have the exact values for the actor attack and enemy defense?
And as gstv87 said, what is the variance?
A critical simple increases the damage
Ruby:
def make_damage_value(user, item)
    value = item.damage.eval(user, self, $game_variables)
    value *= item_element_rate(user, item)
    value *= pdr if item.physical?
    value *= mdr if item.magical?
    value *= rec if item.damage.recover?
    value = apply_critical(value) if @result.critical
    value = apply_variance(value, item.damage.variance)
    value = apply_guard(value)
    @result.make_damage(value.to_i, item)
  end
  def apply_critical(damage)
    damage * 3
  end
So the damage is multiplied by 3. But as suggested if the damage is calculated to 0 * 3 then there is no damage.

If it misses then the damage formula has nothing to do with it. But instead the calculation that is done here.
Ruby:
def item_apply(user, item)
    @result.clear
    @result.used = item_test(user, item)
    @result.missed = (@result.used && rand >= item_hit(user, item))
    @result.evaded = (!@result.missed && rand < item_eva(user, item))
    if @result.hit?
      unless item.damage.none?
        @result.critical = (rand < item_cri(user, item))
        make_damage_value(user, item)
        execute_damage(user)
      end
      item.effects.each {|effect| item_effect_apply(user, item, effect) }
      item_user_effect(user, item)
    end
  end
The critical should only apply if it is a hit.
So now I have to ask, what scripts do you have that works with damage calculations?

class Scene_Battle

alias pc27_crit_effect_show_animation show_animation

posts.author: Roninator2
posts.body:
After doing some testing I found that the PencilCase27 script for critical graphics and sound is
causing the issue.
It does a calculation to determine if the hit will be critical then when the damage is calculated it will recalculate the critical.
I think this script needs to be reworked.
But it can't be recalculated so it needs to have a second method of doing the critical calculation and then if the value is true for the default_crit then it will use the new calculation.
Something like that. And that needs to be done where it does the eval_crit.
Try this instead
Spoiler:
Pencilcase27 critical hit and sound
Ruby:
# Critical Graphics and Sound by PencilCase27
module PC27
  module CrAn
    # use custom critical calculation
    DEFAULT_CRITICAL_CALC = true
    # modification to the critical hit calculation
    # random value * value below < item_cri calculation
    DEFAULT_CRITICAL_MOD = 0.45
    # If this switch is not equal to 0, this switch can be used to turn the
    # animation ON or OFF.
    Switch = 0
    # The two picture id's the script uses to draw the animation. Do not use
    # them for other "Show Pictures" events.
    ActorPicture = 2
    BackPicture = 1
    # Number of frames the image needs to slide in/out
    SlideInTime = 20
    SlideOutTime = 20
    # Number of frames the image stays and distance it moves in that time
    LingerTime = 60
    LingerDistance = 100
    # This is the sound played at the begin of the animation and the number
    # of frames you want to wait before the picture shows up.
    InitSound = "Crit_04"
    InitWait = 30
    # Those are actor specific sounds. It plays one random sound.
    ActorSounds = {
      # Actor_ID => [ "sound1", "sound2", ...],
      1 => [ "Emerald_battle_transition"],
      2 => [ "MavCrit_beginning_of_the_end", "MavCrit_fear_me",
      "MavCrit_gotchya", "MavCrit_lets_finish_this", "MavCrit_many_stars",
      "MavCrit_no_fear", "MavCrit_no_mercy_for_evil", "MavCrit_scatter_to_cosmos",
      "MavCrit_smash_into_space", "MavCrit_stop_wasting_my_time",
      "MavCrit_there", "MavCrit_theres_no_escape", "MavCrit_thisll_hurt_you_more",
      "MavCrit_time_for_final_blow", "MavCrit_unstoppable", "MavCrit_witness_your_demise",
      "MavCrit_you_cant_run_away", "MavCrit_youre_done_for"],
      3 => [ "Pan_Battle_Transition", "Fire1", "Fire2"],
      4 => [ "Tim_Battle_Transition", "CritTim_Prayers", "Fire2"],
    # 3 => [...
    }
  end
end

class Scene_Battle
  include PC27::CrAn
  alias pc27_crit_effect_show_animation show_animation
  def show_animation(targets, animation_id)
    item = @subject.current_action.item
    if item.damage.none?
      targets.each { |target| target.set_crit_to_false }
    else
      targets.each { |target| target.eval_crit(@subject, item) }
    end
    show_critical_animation if actor_crit?(targets)
    pc27_crit_effect_show_animation(targets, animation_id)
  end
    
  def show_critical_animation
    lo = LingerDistance * 0.5
    play_initial_sound
    show_crit_background
    show_crit_actor
    move_crit_actor(Graphics.width * 0.5 - lo, SlideInTime)
    play_random_actor_sound(@subject)
    move_crit_actor(Graphics.width * 0.5 + lo, LingerTime)
    move_crit_actor(Graphics.width + 50, SlideOutTime)
    erase_crit_actor
    erase_crit_background
  end
 
  def play_initial_sound
    RPG::SE.new(InitSound).play
    wait(InitWait)
  end
 
  def play_random_actor_sound(subject)
    RPG::SE.new(ActorSounds[subject.id].sample).play
  end
 
  def show_crit_actor
    name = @subject.name + "CritImg"
    y = Graphics.height * 0.5
    pic = $game_troop.screen.pictures[ActorPicture]
    pic.show(name, 1, -50, y, 100, 100, 255, 0)
  end
 
  def move_crit_actor(x, time)
    y = Graphics.height * 0.5
    pic = $game_troop.screen.pictures[ActorPicture]
    pic.move(1, x, y, 100, 100, 255, 0, time)
    wait(time)
  end
 
  def erase_crit_actor
    $game_troop.screen.pictures[ActorPicture].erase
  end
 
  def show_crit_background
    x = Graphics.width * 0.5
    y = Graphics.height * 0.5
    pic = $game_troop.screen.pictures[BackPicture]
    pic.show("CritBG", 1, x, y, 100, 100, 255, 0)
  end
 
  def erase_crit_background
    $game_troop.screen.pictures[BackPicture].erase
  end
 
  def actor_crit?(targets)
    return false unless Switch == 0 || $game_switches[Switch]
    return false unless @subject.is_a?(Game_Actor)
    targets.any? {|target| target.result.critical && !target.result.missed && !target.result.evaded}
  end
end
 
class Game_Battler
  def eval_crit(user, item)
    @result.critical = false
    @result.missed = (@result.used && rand >= item_hit(user, item))
    @result.evaded = (!@result.missed && rand < item_eva(user, item))
    if !@result.missed && !@result.evaded
      if PC27::CrAn::DEFAULT_CRITICAL_CALC
        @result.critical = (rand * PC27::CrAn::DEFAULT_CRITICAL_MOD < item_cri(user, item))
      else
        @result.critical = (rand < item_cri(user, item))
      end
    end
  end

  def set_crit_to_false
    @result.critical = false
    @result.missed = (@result.used && rand >= item_hit(user, item))
    @result.evaded = (!@result.missed && rand < item_eva(user, item))
  end

  def item_apply(user, item)
    @result.success = false
    @result.used = item_test(user, item)
    if @result.hit?
      unless item.damage.none?
        make_damage_value(user, item)
        execute_damage(user)
      end
      item.effects.each {|effect| item_effect_apply(user, item, effect) }
      item_user_effect(user, item)
    end
  end
end
